Summarise hierarchically coded clinical items

Source: R/desc_coded.r
ks_desc_coded.Rd

Produces a tidy long-format count summary for data coded with a two-level hierarchy, such as MedDRA System Organ Class / Preferred Term (adverse events, medical history) or ATC group / drug (medications).

The function counts distinct subjects (n) and total events (e) at three levels:

  1. Overall total — subjects with at least one record.

  2. Level-1 total (e.g. SOC) — subjects in that top-level group.

  3. Level-2 detail (e.g. PT) — subjects with that specific lower-level code.

The function returns raw counts only; apply ks_n_pct to the n column afterwards to produce formatted "n (pct%)" strings. Rows where <l2> is NA are header / SOC-total rows (i.e. they would be rendered bold in a report).

The function is intentionally single-arm: call it once per analysis population or treatment arm and join the results on the <l1>, <l2>, ord0, and ord key columns.

Usage

ks_desc_coded(
  data,
  id = usubjid,
  l1 = meddra_soc,
  l2 = meddra_pt,
  tot_label = "Total subjects"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble containing the coded event records (one row per event, not one row per subject).

id

<[`data-masking`][dplyr::dplyr_data_masking]> Bare name of the column holding the unique subject identifier.

l1

<[`data-masking`][dplyr::dplyr_data_masking]> Bare name of the top-level code column (e.g. meddra_soc).

l2

<[`data-masking`][dplyr::dplyr_data_masking]> Bare name of the lower-level code column (e.g. meddra_pt).

tot_label

Character string used as the label in the <l1> column for the overall-total row. Default: "Total subjects".

Value

A tibble with one row per display line, ordered by top-level code then lower-level code:

ord0, ord

Integer sort keys. ord0 = 1 / ord = 1: overall total; ord0 = 2 / ord = 2: level-1 (SOC) total; ord0 = 2 / ord = 3: level-2 (PT) detail row.

<l1 name>

Top-level code value. Contains tot_label for the overall-total row; the SOC name for all other rows.

<l2 name>

Lower-level code value. NA for overall-total and level-1-total rows (these are the bold / header rows); PT name for detail rows.

n

Distinct subject count for the group.

e

Event count (number of source rows for the group).

See also

ks_n_pct for formatting n as "n (pct%)" once the population size is known.

Examples

ae <- data.frame(
  usubjid = c("01","01","02","03","03","04"),
  soc = c("Cardiac","Cardiac","Nervous","Cardiac","Nervous","Nervous"),
  pt  = c("Palp","Tachy","Head","Palp","Dizzy","Head"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

## Raw counts (N unknown at this stage)
res <- ks_desc_coded(ae, id = usubjid, l1 = soc, l2 = pt)
res
#>   ord0            soc ord    pt n e
#> 1    1 Total subjects   1  <NA> 4 6
#> 2    2        Cardiac   2  <NA> 2 3
#> 3    2        Cardiac   3  Palp 2 2
#> 4    2        Cardiac   3 Tachy 1 1
#> 5    2        Nervous   2  <NA> 3 3
#> 6    2        Nervous   3 Dizzy 1 1
#> 7    2        Nervous   3  Head 2 2

## Add formatted value column once pop is known
dplyr::mutate(res, value = ks_n_pct(n, totals = 10))
#>   ord0            soc ord    pt n e      value
#> 1    1 Total subjects   1  <NA> 4 6 4 ( 40.0%)
#> 2    2        Cardiac   2  <NA> 2 3 2 ( 20.0%)
#> 3    2        Cardiac   3  Palp 2 2 2 ( 20.0%)
#> 4    2        Cardiac   3 Tachy 1 1 1 ( 10.0%)
#> 5    2        Nervous   2  <NA> 3 3 3 ( 30.0%)
#> 6    2        Nervous   3 Dizzy 1 1 1 ( 10.0%)
#> 7    2        Nervous   3  Head 2 2 2 ( 20.0%)

## Multi-arm via group_modify(); pop looked up per arm
pop <- c(A = 5, B = 5)
ae$trt <- rep(c("A","B"), each = 3)
ae |>
  dplyr::group_by(trt) |>
  dplyr::group_modify(
    ~ ks_desc_coded(.x, id = usubjid, l1 = soc, l2 = pt) |>
      dplyr::mutate(value = ks_n_pct(n, pop[.y$trt]))
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
#> # A tibble: 12 × 8
#>    trt    ord0 soc              ord pt        n     e value     
#>    <chr> <int> <chr>          <int> <chr> <int> <int> <chr>     
#>  1 A         1 Total subjects     1 NA        2     3 2 ( 40.0%)
#>  2 A         2 Cardiac            2 NA        1     2 1 ( 20.0%)
#>  3 A         2 Cardiac            3 Palp      1     1 1 ( 20.0%)
#>  4 A         2 Cardiac            3 Tachy     1     1 1 ( 20.0%)
#>  5 A         2 Nervous            2 NA        1     1 1 ( 20.0%)
#>  6 A         2 Nervous            3 Head      1     1 1 ( 20.0%)
#>  7 B         1 Total subjects     1 NA        2     3 2 ( 40.0%)
#>  8 B         2 Cardiac            2 NA        1     1 1 ( 20.0%)
#>  9 B         2 Cardiac            3 Palp      1     1 1 ( 20.0%)
#> 10 B         2 Nervous            2 NA        2     2 2 ( 40.0%)
#> 11 B         2 Nervous            3 Dizzy     1     1 1 ( 20.0%)
#> 12 B         2 Nervous            3 Head      1     1 1 ( 20.0%)
